pr_body:
Today if `ThreadPool#scheduler` is shut down while submitting a task for
execution by the `MasterService` then we directly throw the rejection
exception to the caller. By the looks of it most callers don't expect
this method to throw anything, so this commit adjusts the behaviour to
fail the task instead.

Closes #105549

review_comments: Why did you need this change for your patch? Trying to connect the dots 🤔

Sorry should have said - the stack trace in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/105549 is kinda useless because it uses `actionGet()` which strips off the outer `ExecutionException` so you can't see who is treating this exception as a test failure.
Should it be more specific and only catch rejection?
I think it can only be a rejection, but there's no good reason to let anything else escape here. I added an assertion in 01e4c816cf3.
